title: Largest Merge Of Two Strings
summary: Given two strings, word1 and word2, construct the lexicographically largest merge by repeatedly appending the first character of either word1 or word2 to the merge string.
statement: Given two strings, word1 and word2, construct the lexicographically largest merge by repeatedly appending the first character of either word1 or word2 to the merge string. Remove the appended character from its original string. Continue this process until both strings are empty, ensuring the resulting merge is the lexicographically largest possible.
constraints: Repeatedly take the first remaining character from either word, preserving internal order in both.
Return the lexicographically largest possible complete merge.
hints: When current characters tie, the larger remaining suffix determines which choice can produce the larger merge.
At each step compare word1[i:] and word2[j:] lexicographically.
Take the first character of the larger suffix, then append whichever suffix remains at exhaustion.
The choice maximizes the first position where the two possible continuations can differ, so it is greedily safe.
editorial: The choice maximizes the first position where the two possible continuations can differ, so it is greedily safe.

tests.explanation: Comparing remaining suffixes at ties yields cbcabaaaaa.
The larger second suffix is chosen through the initial tie, producing abdcabcabcaba.
